chunks: Al-Bazzaz narrated from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Ayyub, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a slave girl who went to a group of people and claimed she was free, so a man from them married her and she bore him a child. Then her master came to them and established proof that she was a slave, and the girl confirmed this. He said: 'She and her child are returned to her master, and it is upon the master to pay her child to his father at his value on the day he returns to him.' I asked: 'If the father has no money to buy his son?' He said: 'The father must strive to raise the price until he pays it and takes his son.' I asked: 'If the father refuses to strive for his son's price?' He said: 'Then it is upon the Imam to ransom him, and he shall not be owned by a free person.'

key_terms.يَوْمَ يَصِيرُ إِلَيْهِ: On the day he returns to him

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a slave girl's child if her master claims her back after she married a free man?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Isfabar highlights the principle of 'Umd al-Banin' (progeny of the father) in Shia jurisprudence, ensuring the child of a free man remains free even if the mother is enslaved. The Imam’s ultimate responsibility to ransom the child underscores the state's duty to prevent the perpetuation of slavery for the offspring of free lineage, preserving social and legal status.
